contexts.stem: "I live in Moscow," he said. Reported: He said he ___ in Moscow. (live)

"I saw him yesterday," she said. Reported: She said she ___ seen him the day before. (see)

"I should rest more," she said. Reported: She said she ___ rest more. (should — no shift)
"I left two hours ago," he said. Reported: He said he had left two hours ___. (deictic shift of ago)
The scientist said that water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius. (boil — universal truth, present preferred)
My friend says he ___ hard every day. (present reporting verb — no backshift) (work)

"Do you speak French?" she asked. Reported: She asked whether I ___ French. (do — reported question)
"We don't have any tickets left," they said. Reported: They said they ___ have any tickets left. (do not — past)
"I am going to apply for the job," she said. Reported: She said she ___ going to apply for the job. (be going to)
"I might travel next summer," he said. Reported: He said he ___ travel the following summer. (might — no shift)
"I have been waiting for an hour," she complained. Reported: She complained that she ___ been waiting for an hour. (present perfect cont. → past perfect cont.)
"Come here and bring this folder," she said. Reported: She told me to go there and ___ that folder. (deictic: bring → ?)
He said he ___ lived in Paris for ten years and still misses it. (mixed backshift — the lived part)
He said he had lived in Paris for ten years and still ___ it. (mixed backshift — current relevance stays present)
Galileo said that the Earth ___ the sun — and the writer agrees it still does. (orbit — present signals agreement)
The ancients believed that the Earth ___ flat — backshift, because the claim is false. (be)
"If I see him, I'll tell him," she said. Reported: She said that if she ___ him, she would tell him. (first conditional backshift)
"If I had time, I would help," he said. Reported: He said that if he ___ time, he would help. (second conditional — unchanged)
He mentioned that if he had known the deadline, he ___ have submitted earlier. (third conditional — unchanged)
"He must be at home," she said. Reported: She said he ___ be at home — a deduction, kept. (must of deduction)
"I'm about to leave," he said. Reported: He said he ___ about to leave. (be about to)
"I will have finished by then," she said. Reported: She said she ___ have finished by then. (future perfect → conditional perfect)
He explained that he ___ been working on the project for months and that the team was finally ready. (sequence harmony — past perfect cont.)
"You needn't come," he said. Reported: He said I ___ need to come. (needn't → didn't need to)
"This morning I overslept," she said. Reported: She said that ___ morning she had overslept. (deictic: this morning → ?)
She just said she ___ leaving — reported moments later, so no backshift. (be, immediate report)
"I ought to apply," he said. Reported: He said he ___ to apply. (ought to — no shift)
"You mustn't touch it," she warned. Reported: She warned that I ___ touch it. (must not, prohibition — stays mustn't)
"I had better leave," he said. Reported: He said he ___ better leave. (had better — no shift)
He said that the treaty ___ flawed — neutral distance, neither agreeing nor stressing it is over. (be — neutral backshift)
He said that the treaty ___ been flawed — marking the judgement as no longer current. (be — past perfect for completed relevance)
Free indirect discourse: Why ___ she said that? Now he would never forgive her. (have — backshifted thought in FID)
"I wish I were taller," she said. Reported: She said she wished she ___ taller. (subjunctive were preserved)
"It is essential that he be present," she said. Reported: She said that it ___ essential that he be present. (main verb shifts, subjunctive 'be' kept)
The prosecution demonstrated that he ___ have been present when the fire broke out. (modal perfect 'must have' — no further shift)
He claimed to ___ seen her the previous day, but the alibi held. (claim + perfect infinitive for past reference)
She recalled that she ___ first met him in Vienna in 1912, long before either had imagined the war. (past-of-past in long passage)

It had long been thought that the manuscript ___ a forgery, until carbon dating proved otherwise. (deep-embedded past)
"The day after tomorrow I fly out," he said. Reported: He said he would fly out ___ days later. (deictic: day after tomorrow → ? days later)

rationale.en: After a past reporting verb the reported clause backshifts one step ({answer} here); exceptions are universal truths, still-relevant facts, present reporting verbs, already-past-perfect, no-shift modals (should/might/ought to), past-form conditionals, preserved subjunctives, and modal-perfects, plus deictic shifts of time and place.
rationale.ru: После reporting verb в прошедшем времени придаточное сдвигается на шаг назад (здесь {answer}); исключения — вечные истины, всё ещё актуальные факты, reporting verb в present, уже-Past-Perfect, не меняющиеся модальные (should/might/ought to), conditionals в прошедшей форме, сохраняемый subjunctive и modal perfect, а также сдвиг обстоятельств времени и места.
